transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, this is the weekly POC sync for NexaHealth. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Jordan Lee: Jordan here.
[00:08] Priya Patel: Priya here.
[00:09] Sam Rodriguez: Sam here.
[00:12] Maya Singh: Maya from Redwood, hi.
[00:15] Alex Chen: Cool. Agenda — onboarding status, access setup, benchmark follow-up, security questions, then next steps.
[00:26] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Quick status from our side: Priya has been working on the service account; ran into some permission bits with our infra team. We don't have the sanitized dataset yet, trying to scrub PHI before we share.
[00:38] Priya Patel: Yeah, small hiccup — the scrub script flagged a few records; will re-run today and aim to hand over a CSV by Tuesday.
[00:44] Alex Chen: Great, thanks. Maya — you had the initial benchmark results from last week's quick run?
[00:49] Maya Singh: Yep. I ran the 100 sample test we talked about — between hosted and a small dedicated pool. Quick caveat — this was with mixed prompt lengths so numbers are noisy. That said, median latency for generation (about 200 tokens) was ~220ms on Dedicated and ~340ms on Hosted in our run. p95 was 480ms dedicated vs 780ms hosted. Cost per 1k tokens ended up lower on Dedicated assuming steady throughput because of reserved capacity math — but of course that's dependent on commit.
[01:22] Sam Rodriguez: Those numbers look promising. Did you run with KV cache enabled? Our workload is heavy on multi-turn clinical notes.
[01:30] Maya Singh: Yes, we enabled prefix caching for those multi-turn flows — it helped a lot. On the dedicated side caching yields ~30% less compute per request for repeated context. There's also quantization options; we tested 4-bit fast quant and saw a small latency drop but need to validate quality.
[01:47] Priya Patel: Quality is important — can you share model accuracy diffs? We can't accept hallucination regressions in clinical summaries.
[01:54] Maya Singh: Totally. I can run a focused eval against your prompt set and highlight any regression. For the quick run the outputs were generally in-line, but I'll give a more formal quality report.
[02:03] Alex Chen: Also, on the security front — Jordan you asked about KMS integration and audit logs?
[02:09] Jordan Lee: Yep. Our security team wants to know if Redwood will let us bring our own KMS and how audit logs are exposed for Private or Dedicated.
[02:18] Alex Chen: Short answer: yes for BYOK KMS in Private and Dedicated, and we stream audit logs to your S3 / GCS or to your SIEM depending on setup. I'll send the SOC2 summary and KMS integration notes after the call.
[02:33] Jordan Lee: Awesome. Any difference in the audit fidelity between Hosted and Dedicated?
[02:38] Maya Singh: Hosted has standard audit logs but Dedicated/Private gives you longer retention and more granular event hooks. Also in Dedicated you can opt for customer-managed logging with our console hooks. Sorry, Redwood Console, to be clear.
[02:52] Priya Patel: On networking — we need specifics for VPC peering vs Private Link. Which does Redwood recommend for us? We run in GCP.
[03:00] Maya Singh: For GCP customers we typically recommend VPC peering for simplicity, but Private Interconnect / VPN are options. For the Private deployment we do VPC peering and route tables, we have a doc with firewall rules and IP ranges. I'll attach that.
[03:13] Sam Rodriguez: Do we need to open outbound ports? Our security team is strict.
[03:17] Maya Singh: Minimal egress needed — for control plane calls and model fetching. We can provide exact CIDR ranges.
[03:23] Alex Chen: Priya, you mentioned permission bits earlier — can you tell us what role you're missing?
[03:28] Priya Patel: The infra team blocked creation of the service account with the custom role we requested. They want a playbook: exactly what permissions Redwood needs.
[03:36] Maya Singh: We'll send a minimal IAM role list — basically storage read only to the bucket with test data, and KMS decrypt if you plan to use BYOK. No admin rights.
[03:46] Jordan Lee: Great. About the benchmark — will you run a 1k prompt test as we requested? We care about p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
[03:55] Maya Singh: Yes, I'm scheduling that. For deterministic numbers we need the sanitized dataset and the service account so we can run from your VPC. If you prefer hosted runs we can run from our hosted infra, but numbers will be different due to network hop.
[04:08] Priya Patel: We'll try to provide service account by Tuesday. If not, run from hosted for an initial comparison.
[04:14] Alex Chen: On dedicated sizing — if the 1k run shows stable throughput, what are the next steps to provision a small dedicated pool for canary?
[04:23] Maya Singh: It's typically a week to provision once contract's signed and we get infra access, less if you already have the sizing confirmed. For a canary we recommend a 2-GPU pool to start, then scale. We'll coordinate with your infra for instance types.
[04:36] Sam Rodriguez: Cost math will be critical for procurement. Can you break down committed vs burst costs?
[04:42] Alex Chen: Yep, I'll include a pricing sheet showing reserved pricing, burst options, and a sample TCO calc based on the benchmark.
[04:49] Jordan Lee: A couple security questions from my team — SAML for SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC granularity?
[04:57] Maya Singh: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning, and RBAC at project and route levels. We can demo the console permissions if you want.
[05:07] Priya Patel: One more — data residency. We process EU patient data sometimes; can Redwood pin instances to regions?
[05:14] Maya Singh: Yes, Dedicated and Private can be region-pinned. Hosted we have region options but you'd want Dedicated/Private for strict residency and compliance.
[05:24] Jordan Lee: Good to know. Anything we should expect in terms of data retention or logs?
[05:28] Alex Chen: We'll share the retention policy. By default hosted logs have 30-day retention; Dedicated can be set to your retention via the console hooks.
[05:36] Priya Patel: Back to the quality checks — if quantization introduces drift, is switching back to FP16 trivial?
[05:42] Maya Singh: Yes, swap is straightforward but will impact latency/cost. We can show you tradeoff curves in the report.
[05:49] Sam Rodriguez: For the canary, we want to run real traffic from a small set of users — can Redwood route only those routes to the dedicated pool?
[05:57] Maya Singh: Yep, route-level canary is standard — route rules, a percent split, and automatic fallback to hosted if needed. We'll show you how to set that in Redwood Console.
[06:08] Jordan Lee: Great. Anything else blocking?
[06:11] Priya Patel: Just the service account and dataset from our side. Procurement and budget are internal but should be moving.
[06:18] Alex Chen: Ok recapping — Alex will send SOC2/KMS notes and pricing sheet; Maya will run the 1k benchmark and share outcome and IAM/VPC docs; Priya will provide svc acct and dataset; Jordan will coordinate procurement. We'll target next sync same time next week, and aim to schedule the canary week of 11/16 pending benchmark and infra access.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:40] Sam Rodriguez: Thanks.
[06:41] Priya Patel: Thanks all.
[06:42] Alex Chen: End call.
